name: Bluetip
label: Dischord
lede: Two Swiz veterans started over in 1995 as The Ohio Blue Tip, went through five drummers in six years, and closed with a record that named Jason Farrell's next band.

eras.title: Swiz kids strike again
eras.text: Swiz was one of the most popular bands in DC's younger hardcore scene of the late '80s, Dischord says. Five years after it ended, Jason Farrell and Dave Stern came back heavier and more rock, and took it straight on the road.

years.h: Two Swiz veterans start over as The Ohio Blue Tip
years.p: [[Jason Farrell|f458f662-c72b-485b-9152-81eda8659fdb]] and [[Dave Stern|636e5c15-b268-404f-8e01-6240caecc53c]] of [[Swiz|eea2f3d8-1e94-436c-ae66-4633f99f55be]] team up with bassist [[Jake Kump|037cdc96-518b-48f4-81bf-3cf095f0de54]] and drummer Zac Eller of Worlds Collide. The name comes from a box of kitchen matches.
years.xp:
Swiz ran from 1987 to 1990, with Farrell on guitar and Stern joining on bass at the end. Wikipedia says the new band began as The Ohio Blue Tip before trimming the name to Bluetip. Dischord dates the start to March 1995.

AllMusic hears [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]], [[Killing Joke|f5aca88c-e3c1-4bc2-af33-68a9a9f7b56a]] and [[Mission of Burma|db9d25d7-a85b-4a29-b2ff-8f5b69ed691e]] in the result. Dischord describes a band with an intense work schedule from the start, and it kept up that pace for the next seven years.

years.h: Bluetip goes into Inner Ear and comes out with Dischord No. 101
years.p: [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] produces and [[Don Zientara|a495882b-4585-4295-9269-e30c63f279fe]] engineers the debut. A Dischord reviewer calls it one of the label's most rock 'n' roll releases.
years.xp:
Thirteen songs, opening with one called "Nickelback." The record is named for its catalog number, which is about as much as the band says about itself on the cover.

Dischord also lists a follow-up release, Past Tense, as No. 101.5.

years.cap: Jason Farrell singing and playing guitar, Washington, DC
years.h: Tool, the Melvins and Hoover take Bluetip on the road
years.p: Wikipedia credits Bluetip's early reputation to those tours. Not the usual company for a Dischord band.
years.xp:
Wikipedia gives no dates for the tours, only that they came during the band's first run. Dischord's own history says Bluetip toured the US, Europe and Japan.

A fan-shot tape survives from an in-store at Extreme Noise Records in Minneapolis on May 27, 1996.

years.h: Zac Eller leaves after the debut
years.p: Bluetip's first drummer goes. Wikipedia lists [[Joe Gorelick|cfc54588-c9b2-4417-bfd8-4a7e4509af3f]] filling in during 1996, then [[Aaron Ford|2e5fcee9-c0bd-4a92-82d1-f76b924b758a]] taking the seat.

eras.title: Join Us, and a revolving drum stool
eras.text: J. Robbins of Jawbox produced the second album, and the sound got sharper. Behind the kit the band kept changing, and Dischord says internal conflicts were part of why.

yt: Melody Bar, New Brunswick NJ, Aug 31 1997
years.h: Sweetbelly Freakdown, the guitarists' other band
years.p: Jason Farrell and Dave Stern also run Sweetbelly Freakdown, which puts out material in 1997, per AllMusic.

years.h: Join Us arrives with J. Robbins at the board
years.p: Recorded at Inner Ear with [[J. Robbins|3babd931-a940-43a8-b629-d7aed5b821d9]] of [[Jawbox|016fba14-1fc6-4986-86c2-2113ec9b28de]] producing and Aaron Ford on drums. Dischord also issued a two-song Join Us single from the same sessions.
years.xp: Dischord lists Join Us under two catalog numbers, 111 and 116, the album and the single.

years.h: Aaron Ford out, Dave Bryson in behind the kit
years.p: Dischord's own history puts it that way. [[Dave Bryson|32151168-adcd-4245-8aba-d8c69a9456a1]] takes over the drums from Aaron Ford.
years.xp:
By Wikipedia's count Bluetip went through five drummers: Eller, Gorelick, Ford, Bryson and, at the very end, Areif Dasha Sless-Kitain. Dischord's shorter version says Eller left after the debut and Bryson replaced him, skipping the middle.

Wikipedia puts the band's eventual end down to creative differences.

eras.title: Polymer, Japan, and Farrell's move to New York
eras.text: With Stern gone and Brian Clancy on second guitar, Bluetip made Polymer and took it to Japan. Then Farrell moved to New York, and the band ended with the move.

years.h: Dave Stern leaves, and Brian Clancy takes his guitar
years.p: Stern goes after Join Us, leaving Farrell and Kump as the only original members. [[Brian Clancy|1a360e20-07fb-4168-a609-f166cd32ced5]] steps in.

years.h: Polymer brings J. Robbins back, this time to Phase Studios
years.p: Dischord No. 121 is cut by Jason Farrell, Brian Clancy, Jake Kump and Dave Bryson. Eleven songs, including "Don't Punch Your Friend (for being slow)."

years.h: US, Europe, Japan: Bluetip plays all three
years.p: Dischord says the band toured all three through its run. The last record even has a song called "Japan."
years.xp: Phantom TV shot a pro set for Space Shower in Japan on October 10, 2000, and it's on YouTube.

years.h: P.M.A. is short for Post Mortem Anthem
years.p: Pieced together from sessions at seven places, from WGNS and Inner Ear to a "Pirate house" and "My House." Track eight, "Retisonic," names Farrell's next band.

years.h: Jason Farrell moves to New York, and Bluetip folds
years.p: Dischord's history is blunt about the cause. Its timeline for the band runs to January 2002.

years.h: Live at the Temple, Dublin, April 17, 2001
yt: Live at the Temple, Dublin, April 17, 2001

eras.title: The song becomes a band
eras.text: Farrell named his next band after a Bluetip song. Years later he and Stern were back with their Swiz bandmate Shawn Brown.

years.h: Retisonic takes its name from a Bluetip song
years.p: Jason Farrell's new band releases the Lean Beat EP. Bluetip also appears on the 20 Years of Dischord set, Dischord No. 125.

years.cap: Jason Farrell playing live with Retisonic
years.p: Wikipedia says Bluetip got back together briefly. AllMusic dates the band's official end to the same year.

years.h: Farrell and Stern form Red Hare with Shawn Brown
years.p: The two ex-Bluetip guitarists join their Swiz singer [[Shawn Brown|e39556a4-0d8f-4138-bc18-a54d3a66eefe]]. Farrell, a working designer, has also put his art on a long list of album covers.
